description: Klee style sequencer: a sixteen place shift register of bits circulates on every clock, and the steps whose bit is set add their knob voltages together and fire three gate buses

params.text: Sets the voltage its step adds to its sum while its bit is set, within the range picked in the menu
Sets the bit its step is given the next time the pattern is loaded
Sends its step to bus 1, bus 2 or bus 3
Loads the pattern buttons into the shift register
While on, the pattern is loaded into the register whenever bus 1 goes active
Shifts the register on by one place by hand
1x16 circulates one sixteen place register; 2x8 circulates two eight place registers, A and B, side by side
Random reads a coin toss into the register in place of the bit coming round; Pat reads the bit coming round, or the feedback taps when those are on
B Inv inverts the bit the B register feeds back into itself, so it alternates; Normal feeds that bit back unchanged; it has no effect in 1x16
The chance of reading in a one while Random is on, 0 to 1
NOR makes bus 2 active only while neither bus 1 nor bus 3 is active; AND makes it active only while both are
Switches the feedback taps on, so the bit read into the register is the exclusive-OR of the tapped steps in place of the bit coming round
Switches on a feedback tap at its step, whose bit is exclusive-ORed into the bit read into the register

inputs.text: Sets its CV knob from the voltage patched here, overriding both the knob and the poly CV input
Each rising edge shifts the register on by one place
A rising edge loads the pattern buttons into the shift register
The random source while Random is on: -5V to 5V is weighed against the threshold, or the menu reads it as a gate above 1V
Sets the pattern bits the next load will use, one channel per step, above 0V for a one
Sends each step to a bus, one channel per step, 0-10V split across the three buses
Switches Random on above 5V and off below
Sets all sixteen CV knobs, one channel per knob, where the step has no cable in its own CV input
Sets the feedback taps, one channel per step, a channel above 1V switching that tap on
Switches the feedback taps on above 5V and off below

outputs.text: The knob voltages of steps 1 to 8 whose bit is set, added together and clamped to -10V to 10V
The knob voltages of steps 9 to 16 whose bit is set, added together and clamped to -10V to 10V
The A sum plus the B sum, clamped to -10V to 10V
The A sum minus the B sum, clamped to -10V to 10V
The B sum minus the A sum, clamped to -10V to 10V
Carries 10V on the channel of every step whose bit is set, sixteen channels wide
A 1ms trigger on the channel of a step whose bit is set, sixteen channels wide
Passes the clock through on the channel of every step whose bit is set, sixteen channels wide
All sixteen CV knob voltages, one per channel, whatever the register holds
Carries 10V while its bus is active, meaning a step assigned to it has its bit set
Passes the clock through while its bus is active
A 1ms trigger when its bus goes active

notes: the shift register comes up empty, so no step is active and no gate fires: set some of the pattern buttons and press Load, or set the Random switch to Random and clock it
menu: Range — the span of the CV knobs: -3V to 3V, -2V to 2V, -1V to 1V, -0.5V to 0.5V, -0.2V to 0.2V, 0V to 1V or 0V to 2V, starting at -1V to 1V
Quantize — rounds the A and B sums to the nearest semitone
Instant mode — recalculates the outputs continuously in place of only on a clock, at about 0.7% more processor load
Ext as Gate — reads the Ext input as a gate above 1V in place of weighing its voltage against the threshold
Randomize CV — gives the sixteen CV knobs new random voltages inside the range set by the Range item
Randomize Bus — sends each of the sixteen steps to a randomly chosen bus
Randomize Load — sets each of the sixteen pattern buttons on or off by a coin toss

inputs.17: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.21: high above 5V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.24: high above 5V · stepped · one channel only
